short: Standard on the encoder: autoencoder features predate it and it is never compared with PCA or DCT; behind on F0, which is copied from the recording, so the listening test is not of a silent system.
position: The paper changes the ultrasound encoder (M06): a one-layer autoencoder bottleneck, stacked over up to 17 frames, replaces raw pixels as input to a spectral DNN. M06 is standard: autoencoder features of tongue images predate it, and its only baseline is raw pixels, not the PCA or DCT coefficients that are the field's usual input and that beat dense autoencoder features in word recognition on the Silent Speech Challenge; no such comparison exists for synthesis. The 25-29% NMSE reduction sets multi-frame autoencoder inputs against a pixel baseline that gained almost nothing from context; at one frame each the gain is 13.5-19.7% relative (inference). M08 is behind the best comparable work: 12 prior studies predict F0 from the articulatory signal, while F0 here is copied from the recording, so the listening test scores a system no silent user could run.
